title: Enhancement of E-commerce Sponsored Search Relevancy with LLM
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of ensuring ad relevance in e-commerce sponsored search by adapting a pretrained Large Language Model (LLM). Specifically, it utilizes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on the LLAMA2 7B model to create an advanced Ad Relevance Classifier. The resulting system significantly improved search accuracy and operational efficiency while offering better privacy compared to existing models like GPT-4.

title: Yambda-5B -- A Large-Scale Multi-modal Dataset for Ranking And Retrieval
summary:
(Abstract fallback)

We present Yambda-5B, a large-scale open dataset sourced from the Yandex Music streaming platform. Yambda-5B contains 4.79 billion user-item interactions from 1 million users across 9.39 million tracks. The dataset includes two primary types of interactions: implicit feedback (listening events) and explicit feedback (likes, dislikes, unlikes and undislikes). title: From Passive Retrieval to Active Memory Navigation: Learning to Use Memory as a Structured Action Space
summary:
1. Current memory systems often passively feed evidence into conversational agents, but researchers propose an alternative approach where long-term user memory becomes an *active*, structured action space for the agent to navigate strategically.
2. The NapMem framework organizes chat history hierarchically (into a "memory pyramid") with linked components like raw conversations and typed records, allowing the agent to be trained via reinforcement learning to select specific memories or granularities relevant to answering questions.
3. Experiments show that using these memory tools through active navigation significantly improves performance on tasks needing long-term user knowledge without impacting general reasoning abilities, suggesting structured memory access is beneficial for personalized agents.
